newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber slow on currency woes, Thai news.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber slow on currency woes, Thai news.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was slow by midday on Monday as the trade was weighed down by lingering worries over the region's currency problems, traders said.
Market players were also concerned about the impact on prices by the Thai government's decision to default on taking delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber last week, they said.

"The market is still worried about currencies and the Thai default. It's a bit slow this morning. The big consumers have not asked for price quotes and they will not do so until later this afternoon," a dealer said.
"It's the same story of wait-and-see. We're also hoping for some leads to come in from Japan," another trader said.
Dealers said they were keeping an eye on Michelin, which was recently engaged in routine purchases for its monthly buying programme, to see if they will come back into the market.
"I understand they'd want to conclude their programme for this month," a dealer said.
At 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 94.00 U.S. cents a kg from 94.75 cents. September RSS1 was indicated at 140.50 Singapore cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg from 139.25 cents.
